_comment: flutter-screen: bending-torsion flutter speed of a uniform cantilever wing — p-k eigenvalue iteration, incompressible strip theory with Theodorsen C(k) (Jones 2-pole), exact uniform-cantilever modal basis. Pure Python + numpy (no meshing, no external solver); runs anywhere numpy runs, so it carries the aces-golden image for consistency with the other pure-python adapters. A SCREEN: the Mach number of the answer is reported beside it, and past Mach ~0.3 the number is indicative, not citable. Validated on the workstation 2026-10-13 against the Goland (1945) wing; the numbers below are the adapter's own docs/validation/flutter-20261013/flutter/flutter.json.

flutter-screen.description: Flutter speed of a uniform cantilever wing from its section properties (EI, GJ, m, I_EA, EA/CG positions, semi-span, chord, density): p-k eigenvalue iteration over a speed sweep, incompressible strip theory with Theodorsen's C(k) (Jones 2-pole rational approximation), exact Euler-Bernoulli/St-Venant cantilever modal basis (n_bending + n_torsion configurable). Reports flutter speed + frequency + the coalescing modes + Mach of the answer, or honestly that no crossing lies in the sweep. Refuses to run with any wing property missing, EA/CG outside [0,1], or fewer than 40 integration stations. Incompressible only: past Mach ~0.3 results are indicative, not citable.

validation.image_id: workstation (pure python 3.11 + numpy 2.4.4; no solver binary involved)

cases.case: Goland (1945) uniform cantilever wing: half-span 6.096 m, chord 1.8288 m, EA 0.33c, CG 0.43c, EI 9.77e6 N m2, GJ 0.987e6 N m2, m 35.71 kg/m, I_EA 8.64 kg m, rho 1.225 kg/m3; 2 bending + 2 torsion modes, 200 stations, sweep 60-180 m/s by 5, bisected crossing
cases.note: expected: Patil et al. (2001) 137.16 m/s / 70.2 rad/s; literature band 135.6-137.2 m/s (Matter 136.41, Bristol binary 137.11). Mechanism is the textbook one: bending frequency rises (46->54 rad/s) while torsion falls (93->69 rad/s) and the torsion-dominated mode's damping crosses zero. In-vacuo bending reference is the Euler-Bernoulli root beta_1 = 1.8751.

validation.note: Ran on the workstation (the adapter is pure python; there is no solver binary to containerise). p-k iteration converged at every speed (pk_converged true). Flutter Mach 0.40: reported with the incompressible-assumption note, as the registry rule requires.
